title: Kedarnath Yatra
alt: Kedarnath temple with the snow-covered Kedarnath peak behind it
summary: The 16 km trek from Gaurikund to the twelfth Jyotirlinga, with acclimatisation built into the itinerary and a night at Sonprayag before the climb.
overview: Kedarnath sits at 3,583 m in the Rudra Himalaya, reached by a 16 km walk from Gaurikund. This six-day itinerary spreads the climb either side of a night at Sonprayag, so you arrive at the temple acclimatised rather than exhausted.
highlights: Overnight at Kedarnath for the morning aarti

itinerary.title: Haridwar to Guptkashi
itinerary.text: Drive along the Alaknanda through Devprayag and Rudraprayag. Overnight at Guptkashi (1,319 m).

itinerary.title: Guptkashi to Kedarnath
itinerary.text: Early drive to Sonprayag, shuttle to Gaurikund, then the 16 km climb. Overnight in Kedarnath.

itinerary.title: Kedarnath darshan
itinerary.text: Morning aarti and darshan, then Bhairavnath temple. The rest of the day is free at altitude.

itinerary.title: Descend to Guptkashi
itinerary.text: Walk down to Gaurikund and drive back to Guptkashi.

itinerary.title: Guptkashi to Rishikesh
itinerary.text: Long drive down the valley with a stop at the Rudraprayag sangam.

itinerary.title: Departure
itinerary.text: Transfer to Haridwar railway station or Jolly Grant airport.

inclusions: All transfers in a private vehicle

faqs.q: How long does the Kedarnath trek take?
faqs.a: Most people take 6 to 8 hours to cover the 16 km from Gaurikund, and 4 to 5 hours coming down. The path is paved stone throughout, so it is stamina rather than technique that decides your pace.

faqs.q: Can I take a helicopter instead of walking?
faqs.a: Yes. Helicopter services run from Phata, Sirsi and Guptkashi and cost roughly 7,500 to 8,500 rupees return. We book slots in advance, as they sell out weeks ahead in May and June.

faqs.q: What should I pack for Kedarnath?
faqs.a: Warm layers including a down jacket, a waterproof shell, broken-in walking shoes, a torch, sunscreen and any personal medication. Nights at the temple drop close to freezing even in June.

title: Badrinath Yatra
alt: The brightly painted facade of Badrinath temple in Uttarakhand
summary: A road yatra to Badrinath with darshan at Mana village, Vyas Gufa and Bheem Pul, comfortable enough for elderly travellers.
overview: Badrinath is the most accessible of the four dhams: the road runs all the way to the temple, so there is no trek involved. That makes this five-day itinerary a realistic option for elderly travellers and families with young children.
highlights: Mana, the last village before Tibet

itinerary.title: Haridwar to Joshimath
itinerary.text: Drive up the Alaknanda valley through Devprayag, Rudraprayag and Karnaprayag.

itinerary.title: Joshimath to Badrinath
itinerary.text: Short morning drive, afternoon darshan and a dip at Tapt Kund.

itinerary.title: Mana village
itinerary.text: Visit Mana, Vyas Gufa, Bheem Pul and Vasudhara falls, then return to Badrinath.

itinerary.title: Badrinath to Rishikesh
itinerary.text: Long descent with stops at the panch prayag confluences.

itinerary.title: Departure
itinerary.text: Transfer to Haridwar or Jolly Grant airport.

inclusions: All transfers in a private vehicle

faqs.q: Is there any trekking on the Badrinath yatra?
faqs.a: None. The road reaches the temple courtyard, and the walk from the car park to the temple is a few hundred metres on level ground.

faqs.q: Is Badrinath suitable for elderly travellers?
faqs.a: It is the easiest of the four dhams. The main consideration is altitude rather than walking: Badrinath sits at 3,133 m, so we build in a night at Joshimath to acclimatise.

title: Chopta - Tungnath Trek
alt: Trekkers on the ridge trail to Chandrashila summit above Chopta
summary: The world's highest Shiva temple, plus a sunrise push to Chandrashila summit for a 360 degree view of Nanda Devi, Trishul and Chaukhamba.
overview: Tungnath is the highest Shiva temple in the world at 3,680 m, and it is only a 3.5 km walk from Chopta. Push another 1.5 km to Chandrashila at 4,000 m and you get a 360 degree view of Nanda Devi, Trishul and Chaukhamba.
highlights: Highest Shiva temple in the world
Runs all year, including snow season

itinerary.title: Rishikesh to Chopta
itinerary.text: Drive through Devprayag and Ukhimath to the Chopta meadows. Evening at leisure.

itinerary.title: Tungnath and Chandrashila
itinerary.text: Pre-dawn start for Tungnath, then the summit push to Chandrashila for sunrise. Descend to Chopta.

itinerary.title: Chopta to Rishikesh
itinerary.text: Optional stop at Deoria Tal on the way down, arriving Rishikesh by evening.

faqs.a: It is one of the gentlest Himalayan treks: 3.5 km on a paved path with a steady gradient, usually 2 to 3 hours up. The Chandrashila extension is steeper and can be icy in winter.

faqs.q: Can I do this trek in winter?
faqs.a: Yes, and many people come specifically for the snow. December to March needs microspikes and proper layers, both of which we arrange.

title: Har Ki Dun Trek
alt: The wide green cradle of the Har Ki Dun valley ringed by peaks
summary: A week in the Govind National Park through Osla and Seema, walking into the valley the Pandavas are said to have taken to heaven.
overview: Har Ki Dun is a wide hanging valley in the Govind National Park, reached through the old wooden villages of Osla and Seema. Seven days at a walking pace, with the Swargarohini massif standing at the head of the valley.
highlights: Ancient villages of Osla and Gangaad

itinerary.title: Dehradun to Sankri
itinerary.text: Long drive through Mussoorie and Purola to the trailhead village of Sankri (1,950 m).

itinerary.title: Sankri to Seema
itinerary.text: Drive to Taluka, then walk 11 km along the Supin river to Seema.

itinerary.title: Seema to Har Ki Dun
itinerary.text: Climb 11 km through Osla and terraced fields into the valley itself.

itinerary.title: Har Ki Dun exploration
itinerary.text: Day walk towards the Jaundhar glacier and the base of Swargarohini.

itinerary.title: Har Ki Dun to Seema
itinerary.text: Retrace the route down the valley.

itinerary.title: Seema to Sankri
itinerary.text: Walk to Taluka and drive back to Sankri.

itinerary.title: Sankri to Dehradun
itinerary.text: Drive out, arriving Dehradun in the evening.

faqs.q: Do I need trekking experience for Har Ki Dun?
faqs.a: No, but you do need fitness. The days are long rather than technical, typically 6 to 7 hours of walking. We ask that you can jog 4 km in under 30 minutes before the trek.

faqs.q: When is Har Ki Dun open?
faqs.a: April to November. April and May bring the rhododendron bloom, September and October give the clearest views, and the valley holds snow into early spring.

title: Valley of Flowers
alt: Alpine flowers carpeting the Valley of Flowers national park
summary: A UNESCO World Heritage site in full monsoon bloom, combined with Hemkund Sahib at 4,632 m for those who want both.
overview: A UNESCO World Heritage site that only opens for the monsoon, when roughly 300 species of alpine flower come into bloom together. The itinerary pairs it with Hemkund Sahib at 4,632 m for anyone who wants the climb.
highlights: Peak bloom in late July and August
Base at Ghangaria in the Bhyundar valley

itinerary.title: Haridwar to Joshimath
itinerary.text: Drive up the Alaknanda valley through the prayag confluences.

itinerary.title: Joshimath to Ghangaria
itinerary.text: Drive to Govindghat, then walk 9 km to Ghangaria (3,050 m).

itinerary.title: Valley of Flowers
itinerary.text: Day walk into the valley, returning to Ghangaria by evening.

itinerary.title: Hemkund Sahib
itinerary.text: Optional 6 km climb to the glacial lake and gurudwara at 4,632 m.

itinerary.title: Ghangaria to Joshimath
itinerary.text: Walk down to Govindghat and drive to Joshimath.

itinerary.title: Return to Haridwar
itinerary.text: Long drive down, arriving Haridwar by evening.

inclusions: All transfers in a private vehicle

faqs.q: When is the best time to see the flowers?
faqs.a: Mid July to late August is peak bloom. The park opens on 1 June and closes on 4 October, but early June and late September have far fewer flowers.

faqs.q: How hard is the walk to Ghangaria?
faqs.a: It is 9 km with a steady climb from Govindghat, usually 5 to 6 hours. Ponies and porters are available at the trailhead if you would rather not carry a pack.

title: Char Dham Yatra
alt: Gangotri temple beside the Bhagirathi river in Uttarakhand
summary: All four dhams in one circuit - Yamunotri, Gangotri, Kedarnath and Badrinath - with rest days built in so the pace stays humane.
overview: All four dhams in a single circuit, in the traditional order: Yamunotri, Gangotri, Kedarnath and Badrinath. Eleven days with rest days built in, because compressing this into seven is how people end up ill at altitude.
highlights: All four dhams in the traditional order
Rest days built in for acclimatisation

itinerary.title: Arrive Haridwar
itinerary.text: Check in and attend the evening Ganga aarti at Har Ki Pauri.

itinerary.title: Haridwar to Barkot
itinerary.text: Drive via Mussoorie to Barkot, the base for Yamunotri.

itinerary.title: Yamunotri
itinerary.text: Drive to Janki Chatti and walk 6 km to the temple and Surya Kund. Return to Barkot.

itinerary.title: Barkot to Uttarkashi
itinerary.text: Drive along the Bhagirathi to Uttarkashi, visiting Vishwanath temple.

itinerary.title: Gangotri
itinerary.text: Drive to Gangotri for darshan at the source temple, then back to Uttarkashi.

itinerary.title: Uttarkashi to Guptkashi
itinerary.text: Long transfer day across the valleys to Guptkashi.

itinerary.title: Kedarnath
itinerary.text: Drive to Sonprayag and climb 16 km to Kedarnath. Overnight at the temple.

itinerary.title: Kedarnath to Guptkashi
itinerary.text: Morning darshan, then descend and drive to Guptkashi.

itinerary.title: Guptkashi to Badrinath
itinerary.text: Drive via Joshimath to Badrinath for evening darshan.

itinerary.title: Badrinath and Mana
itinerary.text: Tapt Kund, Mana village and Vyas Gufa, then drive to Rudraprayag.

itinerary.title: Return to Haridwar
itinerary.text: Final drive down and transfer to station or airport.

inclusions: All transfers in a private vehicle

faqs.q: What is the correct order for the Char Dham Yatra?
faqs.a: Traditionally Yamunotri first, then Gangotri, Kedarnath and Badrinath, moving west to east. Our itinerary follows that order.

faqs.q: How many days does the Char Dham Yatra need?
faqs.a: Eleven days is the comfortable minimum by road. Shorter itineraries exist, but they cut the acclimatisation days, which is where altitude sickness usually starts.

faqs.q: Is registration compulsory for all four dhams?
faqs.a: Yes. Every traveller needs a Uttarakhand Char Dham registration and e-pass, checked at barriers on each route. We file it for you once you send a photo ID.
